item.title: FBI Seizes Virtualine.net in Operation Omegaline Targeting Omegatech
item.content:encoded:
Window: 27 Oct 19:00 → 27 Oct 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Omegatech Is Disrupted, and the Pressure on Bulletproof Hosting Keeps Building — Should Read

Law enforcement’s seizure of Virtualine/Omegatech reflects growing pressure on bulletproof hosting providers, but these operators can rapidly evade disruption by shifting IP ranges and customers to new ASNs and shell companies. Defenders should continuously track infrastructure patterns, newly populated ASNs, and sanctions-linked entities rather than relying on static blocklists.

  • The FBI seized virtualine.net on October 27, 2026, under Operation Omegaline, following an investigation led by the FBI Washington Field Office with law-enforcement partners in Germany, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom.
  • Silent Push observed infrastructure moving from Railnet LLC (AS214943) to Omegatech (AS202412) in February 2026 and identified Virtualine Technologies within Omegatech’s network.
  • Omegatech was not fully offline after the seizure, but its network address ranges showed very low routing visibility, which the article says typically indicates a serious operator-side problem.
  • In 2026, authorities also seized more than 800 servers associated with THE.Hosting/WorkTitans BV and arrested two men, while the EU sanctioned Media Land, ML Cloud, and general director Aleksandr Volosovik.
  • The article states that bulletproof hosting providers can obtain a new network identifier within two to five business days and move the same malicious internet address ranges to it, making static blocklists quickly outdated.

Technologies: cloud-platform, network-monitoring

Products: silent-push-platform, iofa-bulletproof-hosting-feed

Vendors: silent-push, omegatech, virtualine-technologies, railnet, the-hosting, aeza-group, media-land

item.title: Yoba Malware Uses Signed ChatGPT and Claude Installers for DLL Sideloading
item.content:encoded:
Window: 27 Oct 11:00 → 27 Oct 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

An insecure neighbor: how a vulnerability chain led to an isolation bypass in cloud infrastructure — Should Read

A Kaspersky-led bug bounty assessment found that chained flaws in a major cloud provider’s managed Kubernetes and internal management infrastructure could let a normal tenant escape a worker node, compromise control-plane systems, and bypass isolation between tenants. The issues included insecure privileged pod controls, a Konnectivity SSRF-to-RCE path, flat overlay networking, exposed monitoring/logging data, and weaknesses in managed database and SaltStack services; the provider reportedly fixed the findings.

  • Researchers participating in an official bug bounty program found that a managed Kubernetes cluster allowed tenants to create privileged pods with host access, enabling root access to a worker node.
  • A Konnectivity service token found on the worker node could be used with a flaw in the Konnectivity server to make network connections from the Kubernetes control plane and ultimately execute commands there.
  • The provider’s shared overlay network exposed managed-service infrastructure, while VictoriaMetrics and VictoriaLogs endpoints revealed other tenants’ control-plane targets and logs containing root SSH private keys.
  • Researchers identified additional paths to compromise managed Kafka, Redis/Valkey, PostgreSQL, and MySQL services through exposed or improperly configured components, potentially allowing access to other tenants’ data or command execution on their hosts.
  • A vulnerable custom SaltStack script enabled SQL injection against the provider’s cloud-management database, exposing Salt master authentication tokens that could run commands on cloud minions; the provider was notified and fixed the reported issues.

Technologies: cloud-platform, container-platform, orchestration, database, message-queue, network-monitoring, object-storage, backup, operating-system

Products: k0s, kubernetes, konnectivity-server, saltstack, victoriametrics, victorialogs, apache-kafka, redis-exporter, patroni, etcd, valkey, mysql, ubuntu

Vendors: mirantis, kubernetes-project, victoriametrics, apache-software-foundation, valkey-project, oracle, zalando, salt-project

Tricks from the Past deployed via signed ChatGPT and Claude binaries — Should Read

Check Point Research uncovered the Yoba campaign, which uses fake GitHub pages for purported ChatGPT and Claude desktop apps to distribute malware through DLL sideloading of legitimate signed OpenAI and Anthropic executables. The malware persists via scheduled tasks and retrieves attacker-controlled payloads through Telegram-seeded DGA domains and DNS-over-HTTPS, with XMRig cryptomining observed as the final payload.

  • Check Point Research tracked a campaign called Yoba that used fake GitHub repositories and GitHub Pages promoting purported ChatGPT and Claude desktop applications, including GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Claude Opus.
  • The malicious installers packaged a DLL named winmm.dll alongside legitimate signed OpenAI or Anthropic Setup.exe files, allowing the malware to run through DLL sideloading.
  • YobaDropper creates a ProgramData\WMProcess directory, copies the legitimate Windows WMPDMC.exe program there, drops the YobaLoader as wmpdui.dll, and creates a scheduled task running as Local System for persistence.
  • YobaLoader uses a Telegram channel profile image to generate a domain, queries Google DNS-over-HTTPS for a signed and encrypted DNS TXT command, and can download a next-stage payload from Catbox.
  • Researchers observed the loader injecting an XMRig 6.26.0 cryptocurrency miner into svchost.exe, while noting that the loader can also deliver other PE or PowerShell payloads.

Technologies: operating-system, source-control

Products: chatgpt, claude, windows, github, github-pages, google-public-dns, telegram, tor, xmrig

Vendors: openai, anthropic, microsoft, github, google, telegram, catbox, tor-project

Introducing the Cloudflare PHP Capture the Flag challenge — Optional

Cloudflare launched a HackerOne-backed PHP Capture the Flag challenge inviting researchers to bypass its WAF, exploit PHP 8.5.11 vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and retrieve a sandboxed flag. Valid, materially distinct RCE-and-flag-recovery bypasses submitted under the program rules may qualify for a bounty.

  • Cloudflare launched a limited-time PHP Capture the Flag challenge through its HackerOne bug bounty program to test whether researchers can bypass its web application firewall protections.
  • The challenge targets CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 in stock PHP 8.5.11 running with Apache 2 via mod_php in a Cloudflare Container.
  • Participants must use an authorized POST request to achieve attacker-controlled PHP code or command execution, recover the current contents of /flag, and verify the flag through the challenge interface.
  • To claim a bounty, researchers must submit a private, complete, reproducible report to Cloudflare on HackerOne, and awards require a materially distinct bypass method or exploit payload.
  • Cloudflare states that its web application firewall can help protect exposed systems but is not a substitute for applying relevant PHP security updates.

Technologies: waf, container-platform, web-server, cloud-platform

Products: cloudflare-web-application-firewall, cloudflare-containers, php-8-5-11, apache-http-server

Vendors: cloudflare, php, apache-software-foundation, hackerone, emudhra

The Impact of AI on CVEs: INDUSTRY CHALLENGES — Optional

AI is rapidly increasing both legitimate and fabricated CVE reports, overwhelming maintainers and vulnerability databases while making accurate severity assessment and patch prioritization harder. Organizations need to validate real-world exposure rather than rely solely on volume or CVSS base scores.

  • Generative AI is increasing the volume of both legitimate vulnerability discoveries and low-quality or fabricated reports, creating verification burdens for maintainers and vulnerability databases.
  • The curl project ended its bug bounty program in January 2026 after AI-generated submissions contributed to a flood of invalid reports, with confirmed vulnerabilities representing less than 5% of submissions.
  • NIST changed NVD prioritization in April 2026 to focus on CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, federal software, and critical software, while moving older backlogged CVEs to “Not Scheduled.”
  • JFrog found that 54 of 55 advisories published by a newly created GitHub account, including reports targeting SQLite, were fabricated and contained nonexistent code references, impossible line numbers, or unsupported fix claims.
  • AI-assisted discovery is increasing remediation queues, while organizations still need to verify reports, identify affected systems, test fixes, and deploy updates.

Technologies: database

Products: jfrog-xray, jfrog-advanced-security, curl, libcurl, evince, atril, xreader, sqlite, ffmpeg, claude, national-vulnerability-database

Vendors: jfrog, curl-project, gnome-project, sqlite-project, oracle, ffmpeg-project, anthropic

Whole-of-state defense: How SLED agencies can secure critical infrastructure in the AI era — Optional

AI is expanding the cyberattack surface for state, local, and education organizations that operate critical infrastructure, making under-resourced utilities, schools, and local governments attractive entry points. The article advocates a whole-of-state model with shared visibility, governance, services, and prioritized management of IT, OT, identity, cloud, and AI exposures.

  • SLED organizations operate critical infrastructure including water treatment plants, transportation systems, public hospitals, schools, and emergency communications, and nearly 90% of state CIOs rate cyberattacks on critical systems as a high concern.
  • AI expands SLED cyber risk because employees can build unapproved AI-enabled applications, vendors add AI features and connectors that can expand data access, and attackers use automation to conduct reconnaissance faster.
  • Federal agencies warned in July that cyber threat actors were targeting internet-connected operational technology in the water and wastewater sector, including programmable logic controllers whose passwords and IP addresses were altered to lock out operators.
  • A whole-of-state approach treats state agencies, local governments, schools, and utilities as one defensive perimeter through shared governance, visibility of assets and security findings, and cybersecurity services.
  • The article recommends maintaining an inventory of critical assets and AI tools, prioritizing exposures by exploitability and public-safety impact, sharing visibility across jurisdictions, and establishing policies for AI use.

Technologies: ics-scada, plc, iot-device

Products: tenable-one, tenable-one-ot-exposure

Vendors: tenable

Identifying AI agents: Bringing visibility and control to Castle — Optional

Castle has introduced AI-agent identification that uses Web Bot Auth, browser fingerprinting, network signals, and user-agent strings to identify agents such as ChatGPT agent and Perplexity Comet. The company emphasizes that cryptographic authentication offers stronger identity assurance than fingerprinting or user-agent detection, while agent identification remains distinct from bot and abuse detection.

  • Castle has added AI-agent identification that associates identified agent identities with application events and exposes the information through its API.
  • Castle identifies agents using cryptographic Web Bot Auth where available, as well as browser fingerprinting, network-level information, and user-agent strings.
  • Web Bot Auth verifies that requests were signed by a key associated with a known agent operator, while fingerprinting and user-agent strings do not provide the same authentication guarantee.
  • Castle distinguishes AI agents, AI browsers, and browser automation, including agents such as Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Grok Bot, ChatGPT agent, and Instinct, plus Perplexity Comet.
  • Castle states that AI-agent identification, bot detection, and abuse detection are complementary because automated AI-agent traffic is not necessarily malicious.

Technologies: browser

Vendors: castle, meta, openai, xai, perplexity, anthropic

item.title: CVE-2026-111497 Brotli2Shell Flaw Affects Node.js, Envoy, .NET and More
item.content:encoded:
Window: 26 Oct 23:00 → 27 Oct 03:00 UTC (4 hours)

Brotli2Shell: Frequently asked questions for Google Brotli decoder vulnerability (CVE-2026-111497) — Must Read

CVE-2026-111497 (Brotli2Shell) is a critical out-of-bounds write in the Google Brotli decoder that can enable remote code execution when applications decompress attacker-controlled data. Organizations should update affected Brotli-dependent software, including Node.js, .NET, Bun, Envoy, Istio, Python packages, and PHP Windows builds, then restart or redeploy affected workloads.

  • CVE-2026-111497, also called Brotli2Shell, is an out-of-bounds write flaw in Google’s Brotli decoder that Google scored 9.2 under CVSSv4.0.
  • An attacker can trigger the flaw by causing an application to unpack crafted Brotli data, including through compressed HTTP responses or compressed request bodies.
  • Affected software includes Google Brotli, Node.js, Bun, Envoy Proxy, Istio, supported Microsoft .NET releases, Python Brotli packages, and PHP Windows builds, with fixed versions listed in the article.
  • The possible effects range from a program crash and memory disclosure to potential remote code execution, and public proof-of-concept code is available.
  • Organizations should install fixed application releases and restart or redeploy affected processes, containers, and scheduled jobs because updating only a system Brotli library does not fix software that includes its own copy.

Technologies: proxy, orchestration

item.title: PHP2Shell Exploitation, Cloudflare Workers AI Data Exposure, and Supply-Chain Fixes
item.content:encoded:
Window: 26 Oct 19:00 → 26 Oct 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

How to patch PHP2Shell with free Aikido Images — Must Read

Critical PHP2Shell RCE flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) are reportedly being exploited, so organizations should immediately upgrade to fixed PHP releases or use Aikido’s backported container images for unsupported PHP versions and redeploy affected containers.

  • PHP2Shell consists of two critical PHP remote-code-execution flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each rated 9.2 under CVSS v4.0.
  • PHP released fixes on October 21 in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, while PHP 8.1 and older will not receive upstream releases because they are out of support.
  • Cloudflare reports that exploitation of PHP2Shell has started.
  • Aikido provides free patched PHP container images for release lines 5.5 through 8.5, except PHP 8.0, with the PHP2Shell fixes backported for older versions.
  • After switching images, the article recommends rebuilding and redeploying PHP containers, disabling session.upload_progress.enabled, checking public sites with Aikido’s PHP2Shell checker, and looking for signs of compromise.

Technologies: container-platform, package-registry, cloud-platform, web-server

Products: php, aikido-images, amazon-elastic-container-registry, docker, php-fpm, apache-http-server

Vendors: aikido, php, cloudflare, amazon, docker

Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model, and our remediation with SGLang — Should Read

Cloudflare disclosed that a misconfigured KV-cache pool and an SGLang disaggregated-inference bug caused 155 GLM-5.3 Workers AI responses to expose data from recent requests by other customers between August 27 and September 9, 2026. Cloudflare took the model offline, corrected the configuration and engine behavior, restored service, and worked with SGLang on upstream fixes and broader KV-cache safety hardening.

  • Cloudflare disclosed that 155 responses from its GLM-5.3 Workers AI model contained data from other customers’ recent requests between August 27 and September 9, 2026.
  • The exposure occurred only for prompts longer than 681,280 tokens, because the model’s configured 1,048,576-token context window exceeded the capacity of its prefill memory cache.
  • An SGLang disaggregated prefill/decode bug allowed rejected oversized requests to transfer only placeholder data while decode systems read leftover memory pages from earlier requests.
  • Cloudflare disabled the model on September 9, increased the prefill cache capacity to about 2.04 million tokens, patched the inference engine, and restored the model later that day.
  • Cloudflare stated that no other Workers AI model was affected and recommended that disaggregated SGLang operators update to version 0.5.22 or later.

Technologies: cloud-platform, load-balancer

Products: workers-ai, glm-5-3, sglang, mooncake

Vendors: cloudflare, z-ai, radixark, sglang-project, mooncake

eMudhra, Brotli, and the Long Tail of a Security Fix — May Read

Fixing the eMudhra certificate compromise and Brotli flaw requires more than updating Node.js: vulnerable certificate trust paths and bundled decoders may persist across runtimes, applications, and compiled artifacts. Organizations need to inventory what actually shipped, rebuild affected software, and verify that the running application uses the corrected trust store or library.

  • eMudhra disclosed that a flawed key-generation ceremony in April 2025 produced eight intermediate certificate authority private keys that fit within eight bits, making them easy to recover.
  • Chrome and Firefox distributed blocks for the compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates, but other applications may use different certificate stores or verification paths and still trust them.
  • Node.js patched both the eMudhra certificate issue and the Brotli decoding flaw, but updating Node.js does not fix separate bundled or compiled copies in other software.
  • The Brotli flaw, CVE-2026-111497, can corrupt memory when applications decode malicious compressed data and also affected software including Bun, Python Requests installations with Brotli support, and .NET.
  • Organizations should inventory bundled dependencies, rebuild affected artifacts, apply available mitigations, and verify that deployed applications are using corrected decoders and certificate verification settings.

Technologies: browser, operating-system

Products: nodejs, brotli, bun, python-requests, dotnet, golang, firefox, google-chrome, macos

Vendors: emudhra, nodejs, google, oven, microsoft, mozilla, apple, cloudflare

Authorization Differential Testing in Salesforce — Optional

Salesforce authorization should be tested by sending the same request through UI API, GraphQL, and custom Apex, since custom Apex can enforce permissions differently and expose data withheld by native APIs. Review Apex sharing declarations, class API versions, and explicit database access modes—especially for Experience Cloud guest-accessible methods.

  • Authorization Differential Testing compares the same operation for the same user, record, and field across UI API, GraphQL, custom Apex, and other application paths to identify inconsistent access decisions.
  • Salesforce UI API and its GraphQL API enforce the caller’s object permissions, field-level security, and record-sharing access, while custom Apex requires separate review of its authorization behavior.
  • Apex classes using `with sharing` enforce record-level sharing but do not, by themselves, enforce object permissions or field-level security for system-mode database operations.
  • Apex database operations in classes compiled at API version 66 or earlier default to system mode unless user mode is selected, whereas classes compiled at API version 67 or later default to user mode.
  • Experience Cloud guest access to native APIs and to custom Apex methods should be tested separately because guest users may reach different authorization checks through each path.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam

Products: experience-cloud, ui-api, graphql-api, apex, lightning-data-service, lightning-web-runtime

Vendors: salesforce

Socket Threat Intel now shows whether malware campaigns were blocked, detected, or not seen in an organization, with links to the relevant repository scans and Firewall events. The Org Impact view lets teams trace affected package versions to specific repositories, branches, and evidence.

  • Campaign summaries draw on immutable repository scans, pull-request diff scans, and Socket Firewall event traffic.
  • The Org Impact tab lists campaign packages found in an organization, including the repositories and branches containing them and their first and last observed dates.
  • Date links in Org Impact open the associated scan report or matching Socket Firewall events.
  • For campaigns involving multiple packages, Org Impact displays each package and version separately with its own status and first and last seen dates.

Technologies: firewall, source-control

Products: socket-threat-intel, socket-firewall, socket-sca

Vendors: socket

  • The article says attackers use AI to tailor phishing campaigns at scale, while AI agents increasingly read emails, open links and files, and carry out requests for employees.
  • The article states that social-engineering campaigns can move from email into chat threads, shared files, browser tabs, personal accounts, web traffic, and social platforms.
  • Forrester identifies the primary challenge as malicious intent hiding inside legitimate communications, including messages from real colleague mailboxes, familiar vendors, or existing message threads.
  • Varonis says Interceptor tests every message in a sandbox before users or agents interact with it and blocks phishing links from email, collaboration tools, search, ads, and social media.

item.title: LiteLLM Supply-Chain Compromise, PHP CVEs, and Lazarus FlashHole Lead Threat Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 26 Oct 15:00 → 26 Oct 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

LiteLLM Compromise: Coding Agents as the New Insider Risk — Should Read

A leaked master key in an OpenCode agent configuration enabled attackers to steal GitHub tokens, abuse CI workflows to harvest more secrets, and publish the credential-stealing LiteLLM 1.107.0 package. The incident shows that coding agents and unmanaged, long-lived credentials create a major supply-chain risk unless identities are scoped, short-lived, monitored, and kept out of local configs and CI secrets.

  • A master key for LiteLLM’s internal Agent Platform was committed to a public repository in an OpenCode configuration file on May 27 and remained valid for about four and a half months after the commit was removed.
  • On October 10, an attacker used the leaked master key to retrieve managed-agent configurations and obtain a GitHub CLI OAuth token belonging to a LiteLLM GitHub organization owner.
  • The attacker added GitHub Actions workflows that collected and sent repository secrets, including maintainers’ GitHub CLI tokens and database and Redis credentials, to an external webhook service.
  • The poisoned litellm==1.107.0 release was available on PyPI from 11:39 to 13:23 UTC on October 21, 2026, and its Docker images remained available until 14:20 UTC.
  • The malicious package executed code whenever Python started and searched affected machines for cloud credentials, SSH keys, tokens, .env files, shell history, browser passwords, and LLM-provider keys before sending them to an attacker-controlled domain.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control, package-registry, iam

Products: litellm, opencode, github-actions, github-cli, pypi, docker-hub, github-container-registry, cyera-agent-guardian, cyera-identity

Vendors: litellm, github, docker, opencode, cyera

item.title: Infoblox Details Domain Shadowing Abused for Gambling SEO
item.content:encoded:
Window: 26 Oct 11:00 → 26 Oct 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Borrowed Reputation: Domain Shadowing and Gambling SEO — Should Read

Infoblox uncovered two domain-shadowing operations that abused unauthorized DNS records and subdomain delegations under legitimate school and government domains to host illegal gambling SEO pages. Organizations should monitor DNS changes, especially unexpected CNAMEs, NS delegations, and wildcard records, and secure all DNS-management accounts with MFA and auditing.

  • Infoblox identified two unrelated domain-shadowing operations that placed illegal gambling content beneath legitimate school and government domains.
  • Hidden Hawk added individual CNAME records beneath institutional domains, generally pointing the affected hostnames to gambling pages hosted on Cloudflare Pages.
  • A separate operation delegated subzones under maharashtra.gov.in and online.esic.gov.in to ClouDNS nameservers, enabling the operator to manage records beneath those subzones and use a wildcard under gam.maharashtra.gov.in.
  • The primary institutional websites remained available, meaning unauthorized subdomains could evade detection by organizations focused only on their main websites or application logs.
  • The article recommends that DNS operators validate new NS delegations, investigate unexpected subdomains and CNAMEs, review wildcard records, and secure DNS-management accounts with MFA and access-log reviews.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: cloudflare-pages, cloudns, digitalocean, amazon-cloudfront, bunnycdn

Vendors: cloudflare, cloudns, digitalocean, amazon, bunny-net

item.title: ClickFix Brand Abuse, Untested Assets, and AI Agent Security Controls
item.content:encoded:
Window: 26 Oct 07:00 → 26 Oct 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

5 attack chains that started with assets nobody thought to test — Optional

Organizations that focus pentesting only on obvious critical systems can miss overlooked external assets—such as legacy servers, subsidiary platforms, supplier applications, and demos—that provide paths to sensitive data and production controls. The article argues that comprehensive attack-surface discovery and scalable AI-driven testing are needed to identify these hidden attack chains.

  • Research cited by the article found that organizations pentest about 32% of their attack surface on average, leaving roughly two thirds untested.
  • An externally reachable, hostname-less operations server at a transportation company allowed an authentication bypass that exposed live vehicle cargo information and rerouting controls.
  • An outdated analytics server at a global IT services company enabled unauthenticated file reading, disclosure of an administrative password, and a path to a machine in a payment-card environment.
  • A third-party clinical-data application at a pharmaceutical company contained an unauthenticated SQL injection that reached a shared database environment containing 59 databases, including databases of 14 other companies.
  • A public healthcare-platform demo using production application code exposed patient records across four institutions and allowed a low-privilege clinician account to modify records and create non-expiring patient-portal tokens.

Technologies: web-server, database

Products: target-graph, adobe-coldfusion, microsoft-sql-server

Vendors: cycognito, adobe, microsoft

Know How Cyble Brand Intelligence Can Help Stop ClickFix Campaigns in its Tracks — Optional

How to patch PHP2Shell with free Aikido Images — Must Read

PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) is being exploited and requires immediate patching; update to fixed PHP releases or use Aikido’s backported container images for unsupported PHP versions.

  • PHP2Shell consists of two critical PHP remote code execution flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each rated 9.2 under CVSS v4.0.
  • PHP released fixes on October 21 in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, while PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive upstream releases.
  • Cloudflare reports that exploitation of PHP2Shell has begun.
  • Aikido provides free patched PHP container images for most PHP release lines from 5.5 through 8.5, with PHP2Shell fixes backported for unsupported versions.
  • After changing images, organizations should rebuild and redeploy PHP containers, disable session.upload_progress.enabled, and test their public URL with Aikido’s PHP2Shell checker.

Technologies: container-platform, package-registry, cloud-platform

Products: php, aikido-images, amazon-ecr, docker

Vendors: aikido, php-project, amazon, cloudflare

LiteLLM Compromise: Coding Agents as the New Insider Risk — Should Read

A leaked master key in an OpenCode agent configuration enabled attackers to steal GitHub tokens, abuse CI workflows to harvest more secrets, and publish the credential-stealing LiteLLM 1.107.0 package. The incident shows that coding agents and unmanaged, long-lived credentials can create a high-impact supply-chain risk unless identities are scoped, short-lived, monitored, and kept out of endpoint configs.

  • A LiteLLM internal Agent Platform master key was committed in an OpenCode configuration file to a public repository on May 27 and remained valid for about four and a half months after the commit was removed.
  • On October 10, an attacker used the leaked master key to retrieve managed-agent configurations, including a GitHub CLI OAuth token belonging to a LiteLLM GitHub organization owner.
  • The attacker used stolen GitHub access to add CI workflows that collected and sent repository, database, Redis, and maintainer credentials to an external webhook service.
  • The poisoned litellm==1.107.0 release was available on PyPI from 11:39 to 13:23 UTC on October 21, 2026, and its Docker images remained available until 14:20 UTC.
  • The malicious package ran code whenever Python started and searched affected machines for cloud credentials, SSH keys, software-package tokens, environment files, browser passwords, and AI-provider keys before sending them to an attacker-controlled domain.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control, package-registry, secrets-manager, container-platform

Products: litellm, opencode, github-cli, github-actions, github-container-registry, docker-hub, pypi, hashicorp-vault, terraform, kubernetes

Vendors: litellm, github, docker, python-software-foundation, opencode

Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model, and our remediation with SGLang — Should Read

Cloudflare disclosed that a misconfigured KV-cache pool and an SGLang disaggregated-inference bug caused 155 GLM-5.3 Workers AI responses to expose data from recent requests by other customers between August 27 and September 9, 2026. Cloudflare took the model offline, corrected the configuration and engine behavior, restored service, and worked with SGLang on upstream fixes and broader KV-cache safety hardening.

  • Cloudflare disclosed that 155 responses from its GLM-5.3 Workers AI model contained data from other customers’ recent requests between August 27 and September 9, 2026.
  • The exposure occurred only for prompts longer than 681,280 tokens, because the model’s configured 1,048,576-token context window exceeded the capacity of its prefill memory cache.
  • An SGLang disaggregated prefill/decode bug allowed rejected oversized requests to transfer only placeholder data while decode systems read leftover memory pages from earlier requests.
  • Cloudflare disabled the model on September 9, increased the prefill cache capacity to about 2.04 million tokens, patched the inference engine, and restored the model later that day.
  • Cloudflare stated that no other Workers AI model was affected and recommended that disaggregated SGLang operators update to version 0.5.22 or later.

Technologies: cloud-platform, load-balancer

Products: workers-ai, glm-5-3, sglang, mooncake

Vendors: cloudflare, z-ai, radixark, sglang-project, mooncake

Borrowed Reputation: Domain Shadowing and Gambling SEO — Should Read

Infoblox uncovered two domain-shadowing operations that abused unauthorized DNS records and subdomain delegations under legitimate school and government domains to host illegal gambling SEO pages. Organizations should monitor DNS changes, especially unexpected CNAMEs, NS delegations, and wildcard records, and secure all DNS-management accounts with MFA and auditing.

  • Infoblox identified two unrelated domain-shadowing operations that placed illegal gambling content beneath legitimate school and government domains.
  • Hidden Hawk added individual CNAME records beneath institutional domains, generally pointing the affected hostnames to gambling pages hosted on Cloudflare Pages.
  • A separate operation delegated subzones under maharashtra.gov.in and online.esic.gov.in to ClouDNS nameservers, enabling the operator to manage records beneath those subzones and use a wildcard under gam.maharashtra.gov.in.
  • The primary institutional websites remained available, meaning unauthorized subdomains could evade detection by organizations focused only on their main websites or application logs.
  • The article recommends that DNS operators validate new NS delegations, investigate unexpected subdomains and CNAMEs, review wildcard records, and secure DNS-management accounts with MFA and access-log reviews.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: cloudflare-pages, cloudns, digitalocean, amazon-cloudfront, bunnycdn

eMudhra, Brotli, and the Long Tail of a Security Fix — Should Read

Fixing a high-impact flaw such as the eMudhra certificate compromise or the Brotli decoder bug requires more than updating one runtime: teams must find every bundled, vendored, or separately trusted copy across their shipped applications. Effective remediation means rebuilding artifacts, validating the live verifier or decoder, restarting services where needed, and tracking deployment—not merely waiting for a patch to be published.

  • Researchers showed that eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority private keys could be recovered because the supposed 384-bit keys all fit within eight bits, allowing their possible values to be tried by counting to 255.
  • Chrome and Firefox distributed blocks for the compromised eMudhra certificates, but other programs may use different certificate stores or verification methods and can still require updated bundles or verifier changes.
  • The Brotli flaw, CVE-2026-111497, can corrupt memory when an application decodes malicious compressed input, and fixes were released in Node.js, Bun, and .NET.
  • Applications built with bundled runtimes or compiled copies of Brotli, including executables created with Bun's compile feature, require rebuilding because updating a system-installed component does not replace embedded copies.
  • The article recommends tracking bundled dependencies and certificate settings, maintaining automated rebuild paths, testing the actual application verifier or decoder, and monitoring whether patched releases are installed and running.

Even the 'Block this Host' Link Went to the Phishing Page — May Read

A fake Evite invitation sent every link—including privacy, unsubscribe-style, and “Block this Host” footer links—to the same phishing URL, leaving no safe element to click. Users should avoid interacting with unexpected notifications and instead access the purported service directly.

  • A fake Evite RSVP email sent to an employee at a U.S. small-business fintech lender contained 13 links, all pointing to hxxps://aalzntp[.]vu/aut.
  • The links included the RSVP button, privacy and notification settings links, “Block this Host,” “Do Not Sell My Info,” app-store badges, social-media icons, and the postal address.
  • The platform’s link inventory combined the 13 identical destinations into one entry labeled “View & RSVP,” which hid the separate footer-link behavior from reviewers.
  • The email was sent from a legitimate Google Workspace mailbox belonging to an unrelated small business and passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and ARC authentication checks.
  • IRONSCALES classified the email as malicious after its Themis analyst initially flagged it at 50% confidence under the label VIP Recipient.

Kernel eviction notice: What wesp.sys reveals about the Windows Endpoint Security Platform — May Read

Microsoft is developing the Windows Endpoint Security Platform (WESP) to let EDR vendors move much of their monitoring out of third-party kernel drivers, reducing the risk of system-wide crashes like the 2024 CrowdStrike outage. Insider-build binaries show WESP currently uses Microsoft's wesp.sys mini-filter and espclient.dll to deliver filtered security events to user-mode clients, though user-mode blocking decisions do not yet appear implemented.

  • Microsoft is developing the Windows Endpoint Security Platform (WESP) to move EDR product functionality from third-party kernel drivers into user mode while retaining a Microsoft-maintained kernel component.
  • The initiative follows the July 19, 2024 CrowdStrike outage, in which a bad configuration-file update caused CrowdStrike's EDR kernel driver to crash millions of Windows machines.
  • Windows Insider builds include the WESP kernel driver wesp.sys and the user-mode API library espclient.dll, although the platform is not publicly documented.
  • Analysis of wesp.sys shows that it is a file-system mini-filter at altitude 329500 that communicates with user-mode clients through a FilterCommunicationPort named ESPFilterPort.
  • The espclient.dll exports functions related to filters, rules, and event queues, but its imports do not include FilterReplyMessage, suggesting user-mode clients may not currently be able to return decisions such as blocking process creation.

Technologies: operating-system, edr, xdr

Products: windows, windows-endpoint-security-platform, wesp-sys, espclient-dll, elastic-defend

Vendors: microsoft, crowdstrike, elastic

Authorization Differential Testing in Salesforce — Optional

Salesforce authorization can differ between UI API/GraphQL and custom Apex, so the same restricted user may receive data through Apex that native APIs correctly withhold. Test identical requests across all exposed paths, especially Experience Cloud guest flows, and explicitly review Apex sharing, API version, and user- versus system-mode database access.

  • Authorization Differential Testing compares the same user, record, field, and operation across UI API, GraphQL, custom Apex, and other application paths to identify inconsistent access decisions.
  • Salesforce UI API and its GraphQL API apply the caller’s object permissions, field-level restrictions, and record-sharing access when returning supported record data.
  • Apex classes compiled at API version 66 or earlier use system-mode database operations by default unless user mode is explicitly selected, while classes compiled at version 67 or later use user context by default.
  • Apex declared "with sharing" enforces record-level sharing but does not by itself enforce object permissions or field-level restrictions for system-mode database operations.
  • Experience Cloud guest access to native public APIs and guest access to custom Apex classes are separate controls that should be tested independently.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam

Products: salesforce, experience-cloud, ui-api, graphql-api, lightning-web-runtime, lightning-data-service, apex

Vendors: salesforce, netspi

5 attack chains that started with assets nobody thought to test — Optional

Organizations often leave low-priority external assets—such as legacy servers, subsidiary systems, supplier applications, and demos—untested, even though they can provide paths to critical systems and sensitive data. The article argues that comprehensive attack-surface discovery and scalable AI-driven pentesting can uncover these overlooked attack chains.

  • Research from Synack and Omdia found that organizations pentest about 32% of their attack surface on average, leaving roughly two thirds untested.
  • An IP-only homegrown transportation application allowed unauthenticated access to live vehicle cargo data and controls that could reroute vehicles because a crafted web address bypassed its login gateway.
  • A legacy analytics server at a global IT services company exposed an administrative password through manipulated XML requests, enabling system-level access and a potential foothold into a PCI-scoped environment.
  • A supplier-built clinical-data application at a pharmaceutical company contained an unauthenticated SQL injection path to a shared database server with 59 databases, including databases belonging to 14 other companies.
  • The article argues that organizations need complete external attack-surface discovery and scalable testing to investigate overlooked assets such as legacy systems, subsidiaries, supplier applications, and public demos.
